## 固定收益開盤主論

全球半導體類股重挫、油價下跌，加上市場質疑聯準會升息時點，促使買盤在前一交易日美債遭到拋售後回流，6月23日美債小幅上漲。2年期殖利率下降2.9個基點至4.199%，5年期下降1.9個基點至4.269%，10年期下降1.2個基點至4.498%，30年期微降0.2個基點至4.947%。前端領漲使2s10s陡峭化1.7個基點至29.9個基點，2s30s則陡峭化2.7個基點至74.8個基點。

相較於股市受到的衝擊，美債漲勢仍顯克制。那斯達克100指數下跌3.29%，費城半導體指數重挫7.87%，標普500指數下跌1.44%，VIX則上升12.79%至19.49。南韓Kospi指數已先行下跌10%，槓桿部位賣壓又放大三星電子與SK海力士的跌勢。美債獲得避險買盤，但市場並未放棄聯準會更具限制性的政策路徑：交換市場仍反映截至2027年年中約45個基點的升息幅度，美元指數也上漲0.39%至7個月高點。

油價則從另一條管道帶來緩解。美國與伊朗達成臨時和平安排後，通過荷莫茲海峽的油輪活動變得更為明顯，WTI下跌2.15%至$73.21，布蘭特原油下跌1.05%至$77.08。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點至2.219%，10年期實質殖利率卻上升1.8個基點至2.279%。因此，名目美債上漲是因通膨補償的降幅超過實質殖利率的升幅；這種組合反映未來能源壓力減輕，但投資人仍要求偏高的通膨調整後報酬。

最新美國調查未能化解這項拉鋸。6月標普全球綜合PMI初值升至52.2，主要由製造業帶動；然而，就業連續第2個月下滑，工廠裁員幅度更是2020年以來最大。區域調查較弱，交貨延遲與銷售價格指標仍令重新聚焦恢復物價穩定的聯準會感到不安。交易員降低了對近期最激進升息情境的押注，但未排除今年稍後升息的可能性。

初級市場也凸顯同一差異。規模$690億的2年期美債標售以4.189%得標殖利率吸引強勁需求；SpaceX則必須相對可比投資級債支付顯著溢酬，才完成首筆$250億債券發行。兩筆交易顯示，投資人願意在新的殖利率結構下投入資金，但企業債投資人仍要求取得補償，因為股權估值本身無法消除現金流風險。

## 風險趨避帶動美債有限反彈

美債行情始於全球科技股交易迅速惡化。南韓股市原先僅溫和下跌，後來演變成Kospi指數重挫10%，並觸發熔斷機制；外資賣超逾$25億股票。三星電子與SK海力士跌幅均超過12%，市場人士認為，槓桿散戶遭強制平倉，以及與槓桿型交易所交易產品相關的賣盤，是跌勢擴大的原因。

壓力隨後蔓延至美國晶片製造商。半導體指數自戰爭引發的低點以來已上漲逾一倍，此次下跌近8%；美光科技在預定6月24日公布財報前重挫13%。那斯達克100指數下跌3.3%，轉為當週下跌，但今年以來仍維持上漲。這更像是先前大漲後的劇烈反轉，本身不足以證明整體經濟正在收縮。

這項催化因素之所以牽動債市，是因投資人同時重新評估人工智慧支出的預期報酬，以及折現這些報酬所採用的利率。科技業原本受惠於市場對龐大基礎建設需求的期待，但聯準會升息預期升高，使對利率敏感的股票估值更難維持。這波拋售因而為美債帶來避險買盤，也顯示FOMC會議後實質殖利率上升，已使金融情勢收緊。

SpaceX股價充分反映這種不穩定。盤中一度下跌4.8%、也曾上漲7.1%，終場上漲1%至$156.11。這波漲勢終止了連續3天、蒸發逾$6,000億市值的跌勢，卻未消除市場對人工智慧、衛星及軌道運算計畫所需融資的廣泛疑慮。

相較於股票，信用債基金價格較為穩定。投資級債基金LQD上漲0.12%，HYG與JNK則分別下跌0.09%及0.05%；新興市場債基金EMB下跌0.15%。這些變動幅度有限，顯示截至收盤，科技股衝擊尚未演變為上市債券基金的全面無差別拋售。

風險行情反轉之際，美債成交量同步增加。FINRA記錄的面額交易量達$1.132兆，較6月22日增加14.2%；名目附息債交易量增加16.1%至$8,557億，其中剩餘期限不超過2年的名目附息債交易量增加35.5%至$2,398億。這些數字衡量的是雙向交易而非投資人方向，但成交集中於前端，與當日市場重新評估聯準會行動時點及2年期新債標售相符。

殖利率曲線的變化只是部分扭轉前一週的趨平走勢，並不代表市場重回寬鬆政策展望。2年期殖利率當週仍上升14.4個基點，相較之下，10年期上升5.8個基點，30年期僅上升0.3個基點。同期間2s10s仍趨平8.6個基點，過去1個月則趨平13.7個基點。

選擇權交易說明了現券漲勢為何保持溫和。聯準會6月決策公布後，擔保隔夜融資利率期貨交易量立即增加一倍，許多部位押注升息次數將少於貨幣市場逐漸反映的幅度，相關交易延續至本週。道明證券策略師Molly Brooks認為，即使今年稍後升息仍有可能，市場預期最快7月升息仍過度激進，因決策官員可以等待更多勞動與通膨證據。

投資人也買進可在美債更大幅上漲時獲利的選擇權。週一及週二合計投入近$3,000萬買進8月買權；若10年期殖利率朝4.4%或更低水準移動，這些部位即可受益。摩根大通客戶調查顯示，美債中立部位比重上升4個百分點，達約2個月最高；多頭與空頭比重則各下降2個百分點。這種組合更能說明投資人對升息時點的不確定，而非全面否定聯準會轉向鷹派。

美元強勢則呈現政策訊號的另一面。彭博美元現貨指數上漲0.4%，收在去年11月以來最高點，主要受到市場預期聯準會截至2027年初可能升息近兩次、每次25個基點，以及其他經濟體政策預期較弱支撐。歐元一度跌至$1.1376，日圓則貶破每美元160日圓後持續承壓。美債與美元同步上漲，因此符合風險趨避行情：美國利率預期僅由高檔小幅下修，相對其他經濟體仍然偏高。

油價下跌降低了聯準會立即回應的一項理由。荷莫茲海峽的油輪活動更為明顯，顯示臨時和平安排正在改善實體運輸；美國也向伊朗核發為期60天的國際石油銷售許可。不過，外交協商尚未完成。美國總統Donald Trump表示，預計從伊朗遭凍結帳戶釋出的$120億只能用於向美國購買食品及醫療用品；伊朗官員則稱這筆資金可自由運用。伊朗與阿曼也表示，將研議未來的海峽管理安排，其中仍未解決的議題包括是否徵收過境費。

市場把這些爭議視為供應情勢改善的保留條件，而非運輸再度中斷。油價走低使WTI過去1個月累計下跌24.21%，布蘭特原油下跌25.56%。黃金期貨下跌1.24%至$4,129.90，月跌幅擴大至8.65%；偏高的實質殖利率與走強的美元，抵銷了當日的避險需求。

## 商業調查顯示產出加快、勞動轉弱

6月美國PMI初值提供了最強的當期景氣訊號。綜合產出指數由51.5升至52.2，高於50代表擴張。服務業商業活動指數由50.7升至51.3，製造業PMI由55.1升至55.7，製造業產出指數也由56.6升至57.7。

但產出加快並非全面令人安心。整體調查的就業連續第2個月下滑，工廠人力更以2020年以來最快速度縮減。供應商交貨延遲的普遍程度為2022年8月以來最高，反映供應持續受阻及企業建立庫存。投入成本通膨僅由高檔小幅降溫，產出價格通膨則維持在5月的偏高速度。

這種組合之所以攸關政策反應，是因產出加速並未帶來更強的就業或更明確的通膨降溫。製造商受惠於需求與預防性庫存累積，但交貨時間拉長、銷售價格仍高，意味供應壓力可能持續。另一方面，就業下滑也不支持把工廠生產增強視為立即升息的充分證據。

區域報告更明確偏向活動放緩。里奇蒙聯準銀行6月製造業綜合指數由13降至4；出貨指數由16降至3，新訂單由17降至9，就業由3降至-1。當地商業情勢由5轉為-3，陷入負值，但未來當地情勢預期由17改善至23。未來就業預期則由23降至16，企業並回報支付價格明顯加速。

費城聯準銀行非製造業調查呈現另一種組合。企業層級的一般活動指數由-3.8轉為2.4，銷售或營收由-7.6反彈至19.6。新訂單仍略為負值，由-0.8微升至-0.7；全職就業則由-1.1惡化至-4.8，企業未來6個月展望更由14.4降至-0.3。

該調查的價格指標方向分歧：支付價格由36.5降至25.8，收取價格卻由13.1升至20.2；區域一般活動指數則由-23.6進一步降至-25.8，維持深度負值。因此，企業銷售回升同時伴隨招聘轉弱、展望惡化及實際銷售價格走強。

整體而言，這些數據並未提供單一的成長或通膨訊息。全國PMI顯示景氣擴張加快，尤以製造業為主；里奇蒙報告呈現廣泛減速；費城服務業調查則顯示銷售改善，但訂單與勞動未同步增強。各報告的共同點是就業疲弱，而對債市較不利之處，在於即使油價下跌，價格壓力仍清楚可見。

這種分歧有助解釋短天期美債為何表現較佳，整體債市卻未出現更大漲幅。招聘轉弱與區域需求不均，使立即升息的理由受到挑戰；但偏高的產出價格、供應延遲及里奇蒙支付價格加速，仍支持維持限制性政策。截至2027年年中市場仍反映約45個基點的升息幅度，這次調整主要針對聯準會何時行動，而非認為通膨風險已經消失。

10年期殖利率的通膨拆解更凸顯這項差異。隨油價回落降低對未來物價上漲的補償需求，10年期損益兩平通膨率降至2.219%，當週下跌8.7個基點、過去1個月下跌19.4個基點。10年期實質殖利率卻升至2.279%，當週上升14.5個基點、過去1個月上升13.3個基點。投資人雖降低了10年期名目債所附加的通膨溢價，但相較6月政策重新定價之前，仍要求高出許多的實質報酬。

## 前端殖利率升高，美債標售仍見需求

規模$690億的2年期公債標售，最清楚顯示買方願意在目前水準增加政策敏感型債券部位。得標殖利率為4.189%，低於投標截止前市場預期的殖利率，反映需求強勁；但這仍是2025年1月以來最高的2年期標售殖利率。

這次標售距聯準會主席Kevin Warsh首次會後記者會不到一週。該場記者會推動前端殖利率大幅上升，促使市場反映未來一年接近50個基點的升息幅度。截至6月23日收盤，2年期殖利率約為4.20%，標售水準與當時市場接近，但殖利率已足以吸引認為升息路徑可能不如市場近期定價般激進的投資人。

這是連續3天固定利率附息債標售的第一筆。財政部預定6月24日標售$700億新發行5年期債券，6月25日再標售$440億新發行7年期債券。2年期結果證實，與政策利率關聯最直接的期限具有需求；但尚無法判斷投資人是否同樣青睞殖利率曲線中段，因期限溢價、實質殖利率與企業避險在該區段可能發揮更大作用。

這項差異在標售週期開始前便已浮現。儘管油價下跌，5年期與10年期殖利率仍在6月22日上升，交易員認為部分走勢源自SpaceX巨額債券融資相關的利率避險。大型公司債定價前，這類避險可能暫時增加美債賣壓。融資與2年期標售完成後，壓力已有所緩和；但即將登場的5年期及7年期標售，仍使曲線中段面臨進一步供給考驗。

財政部另一筆$650億、42天期國庫券標售的最高利率為3.620%，投資利率為3.686%，投標倍數為2.91倍。間接投標人獲配競爭性投標得標量的65.67%，一級交易商取得32.04%，直接投標人取得2.29%；財政部對以最高利率提交的投標分配92.35%。

這項結果顯示6週期券供給獲得承接；但因缺乏發行前交易參考殖利率，無法判斷標售是否出現尾差或低於發行前水準。證券將於6月25日交割及發行，並於8月6日到期。這筆標售增加$650億短期國庫券供給，但沒有顯示前端融資壓力，也未與附息債的溫和漲勢相抵觸。

現券市場活動也顯示，當日行情不只是標售機制造成。多個期限區段的名目附息債面額交易量均增加，其中剩餘期限超過3年至5年的交易量上升10.9%，20年以上上升16%；TIPS交易量增加4.7%至$288億。成交量廣泛增加，同時伴隨股市衝擊、政策重新定價及初級市場供給，而非只反映單一標售結果。

## SpaceX首度發債250億美元，以溢酬換取需求

SpaceX透過5個投資級債券券次募得$250億，將前一天的市場推介轉化為史上規模最大的企業首次發債案之一。需求最高時接近$900億，定價時約為$730億。最終訂單簿不到發行規模的3倍，低於今年高評級債券交易約4倍的平均水準。

該公司2036年到期債券的利差較美債高1.4個百分點，較同評等BBB債券平均利差寬約0.4個百分點。這項發行溢酬顯示，即使SpaceX具投資級評等、股權價值約$2兆，也無法消除債權人對其資本計畫規模與持續時間的疑慮。

最短天期、風險最低的券次需求最強，符合固定收益投資人的主要顧慮。債券持有人可領取票息與本金，但即使衛星網路、人工智慧或太空資料中心創造極為可觀的股權報酬，也無法充分分享上行利益；若建設成本上升、現金流產生時間晚於預期，或公司選擇優先維持擴張計畫，而非按債權人偏好的速度降槓桿，債權人仍須承擔下行風險。

信用評等提供一定空間，但評等機構對風險並無一致看法。穆迪給予SpaceX Baa1評等，與近10年前首次給予輝達的評等相同；當時輝達負債較輕，且自由現金流為正。標普預期SpaceX到2030年仍將持續消耗現金，並因支出增速快於營收，現金消耗速度會在2027年大幅加快。

截至6月19日，SpaceX持有逾$1,000億現金，並表示有意維持投資級評等。評等機構列出的潛在防禦措施包括放慢投資速度或增發股權。這些選項可降低近期流動性風險，卻無法消除公司實現其雄心最終需要舉債多少的不確定性。

儘管如此，訂單簿仍證明SpaceX具備龐大的融資能力。在科技股大跌、美債實質殖利率維持高檔，且市場對人工智慧估值的疑慮跨區域擴散之際，投資人仍承接$250億債券。融資窗口確實開啟；2036年期債券相對美債的140個基點利差，就是以如此龐大規模使用該窗口的代價。

其他科技公司債近期表現也促使買方保持審慎。輝達前一週募得$250億，最高吸引$850億訂單，但其債券之後相對美債略為轉弱。SpaceX最終認購倍數較低，投資人又偏好最短天期券次，顯示買方正在區分不同科技業借款人，而非把人工智慧題材本身視為充分的信用支撐。

SpaceX股債市場的對比尤其鮮明。其股價在連跌3天後於6月23日回升1%，但盤中波動仍大。股東可以評估公司實現超常成長的機率；債權人關注的則是契約現金流、槓桿，以及各項計畫產生報酬所需的時間。相較於股價，債券溢酬更直接反映這種不對稱性。

## 歐洲與日本面臨不同的通膨約束

歐元區數據顯示經濟萎縮程度減輕，但尚未恢復成長。6月綜合PMI初值由48.5升至49.5，仍連續第3個月低於50。服務業指數由47.7改善至48.9，製造業PMI則由51.6降至51.3，製造業產出指數由51.3微降至51.2，就業也小幅下滑。

相較於景氣復甦，價格壓力降溫更為明顯。投入成本通膨放緩至2月以來最低，產出價格通膨則是3個月最低。這種組合促使交易員降低歐洲央行升息預期，也對歐元構成壓力；但決策官員仍警告，累積的能源衝擊可能使通膨到2027年仍高於目標。

歐洲央行首席經濟學家Philip Lane表示，前瞻指標顯示未來幾個月仍有價格壓力，通膨可能在「相當長一段時間」維持於2%以上。他表示，即使在歐洲央行較溫和的中東情境下，6月升息仍是審慎的回應。Lane也指出，薪資仍有一定動能，今年平均每位勞工的薪資增幅可能高於通膨，但他承認經濟成長風險偏向下行。

副總裁Boris Vujcic為6月升息辯護，認為在歐洲央行各種情境下，整體與核心通膨預計都將在更長時間內維持較高，因此這項決定相當穩健。不過，他也指出中長期通膨預期仍受控，平均每位員工薪酬增速正在放緩，目前沒有證據顯示薪資造成第二輪效應。

西班牙央行總裁Jose Luis Escrivá則強調另一條傳導管道。他表示，石油成本已沿生產鏈傳導至運輸、食品及其他商品，政策必須考量這對通膨中較持久成分直至2027年的影響。這番談話再次凸顯，當前商業活動雖較弱，通膨過程卻可能延續至最初能源衝擊之後。

政策訊息分歧，使歐洲與聯準會的差異更為擴大。美元指數升至7個月高點，歐元盤中則跌至約1年最低。1年期歐元兌美元風險逆轉指標顯示，市場對歐元賣權的偏好升至2025年美國宣布關稅前以來最強。即使歐洲央行官員尚未宣告緊縮工作完成，匯市仍認為美國利率相對歐元區利率上升的機率更高。

匈牙利則朝相反方向行動。匈牙利國家銀行將基準利率下調25個基點至6%，符合21位經濟學家中20位的預測。總裁Mihaly Varga表示，決策官員可在夏季再降息兩次、每次25個基點，並於9月重新評估政策空間；他把這一連串行動稱為「迷你」寬鬆週期。

該央行把2026年平均通膨預測由3月估計的3.8%下調至1.8%，預期通膨將於2027年升至2.3%，並在2028年達到3%目標。福林走強降低輸入性通膨，使匈牙利即使面對整體能源衝擊，仍能採取有別於歐洲央行與捷克央行的政策。

決策公布後，福林兌歐元一度下跌1.3%，創3月以來最大跌幅，今年以來升幅也縮至約8%。即使降息，匈牙利6%的基準利率仍遠高於波蘭及捷克的3.75%。市場反應顯示，寬鬆空間部分取決於能否守住原先創造該空間的匯率漲幅。

日本公債市場則發出較不理想的需求訊號。5年期JGB標售投標倍數為3.11倍，低於前次的3.22倍及過去12個月平均的3.47倍；標售尾差由0.04擴大至0.06，結果公布後債券期貨也收斂漲幅。

這次需求偏弱之際，日圓已貶破每美元160日圓，投資人也在評估日本央行是否必須再次升息以抑制輸入性通膨。隔夜指數交換市場反映，2026年剩餘時間內升息幅度不到一次25個基點。標售結果顯示，買方仍要求取得補償，以承擔日圓疲弱與通膨持續迫使日本央行加快升息的風險。

歐洲一項假設性的監管變動，則為美債帶來另一個結構性議題。基爾研究所經濟學家的研究估計，若對歐洲銀行與保險公司持有的美國政府債券施加20%風險權重，未來10年需求可能減少約$2,000億，並因殖利率上升，使美國每年財政成本最多增加$420億。這只是研究情境，並非已宣布的政策；但它量化了監管待遇如何影響海外需求基礎，而不必假設各國主權投資人協同行動拋售美債。

## 後市意義

澳洲5月月度CPI將於6月24日雪梨時間11:30公布。前次數據顯示物價較上月上升0.4%、較一年前上升4.2%。整體及截尾平均通膨將決定能源價格回落是否帶來足夠緩解，從而支持澳洲央行維持限制性立場。

美國新屋銷售將於美東時間10:00公布。4月年化銷售速度為62.2萬戶，待售庫存48.9萬戶，供應量相當於9.4個月。這份報告將更新偏高房貸利率對需求、房價與住宅庫存的影響。

財政部6月24日的供給首先是美東時間11:30增額發行$280億2年期浮動利率債券，利差為0.103%，6月26日交割；同一時間也將標售119天期國庫券。更大的考驗在13:00，屆時財政部將標售$700億、2031年6月30日到期的新發行5年期債券。結果將顯示，2年期標售呈現的需求能否延伸至同時承受較高實質殖利率及企業利率避險影響的區段。

日本將於6月25日增額發行約¥7,000億20年期JGB，結果預計在東京時間12:35左右公布。這次標售緊接著需求較弱的5年期標售，將檢驗市場對日本央行政策路徑與日圓貶值的疑慮，是否在超長天期區段引發更強阻力。

美國主要數據將集中在6月25日美東時間08:30公布。初領失業救濟金人數預估為22.5萬人，前值22.6萬人；續領人數前值為181萬人。數據將有助判斷，6月商業調查反映的就業疲弱是否已出現在裁員，或仍集中於招聘與企業人力配置計畫。

5月耐久財訂單初值預計下降5%，前月為上升7.9%。運輸項目可能主導整體數字，因此扣除運輸與資本財的細項更能反映企業投資。第1季GDP第3次估值預計為年化成長1.7%，前次為1.6%；PCE價格修正則將進一步釐清通膨起點。

個人所得與支出對政策最具意義。市場預期所得增加0.4%、支出增加0.6%，整體PCE價格月增0.5%，核心PCE價格月增0.3%。若核心數據穩健且實質支出展現韌性，將支持聯準會的限制性傾向，並對押注升息次數較少的選擇權部位構成挑戰。若通膨或消費較弱，尤其同時伴隨勞動市場轉弱的證據，則會強化延至7月以後再行動的理由。

財政部將於6月25日美東時間13:00，以$440億、2033年6月30日到期的新發行7年期債券，完成本輪附息債標售；4週及8週期國庫券則先於11:30標售。5年期與7年期標售的投標人參與程度及交易商獲配比重，將顯示週二的前端需求是否僅限特定期限，或反映投資人普遍願意在目前殖利率附近承接債券。

墨西哥央行將於6月25日美東時間15:00公布6月利率決策。目前隔夜目標利率為6.50%，市場預期維持不變。能源通膨、披索對美元走強的敏感度，以及全球政策轉向緊縮，將決定央行是否繼續把寬鬆週期視為已經結束。

密西根大學6月消費者調查終值將於6月26日美東時間10:00公布。初值顯示信心指數為48.9，現況指數48.4，預期指數49.3。信心與通膨預期的修正，將顯示油價下跌是否開始改善家庭看法，或先前的價格衝擊是否仍根深蒂固。

半導體類股重挫後，美光財報構成較近的市場考驗。獲利與需求評論將顯示，這波賣壓究竟反映市場重新評估人工智慧基礎建設訂單，還是主要源自槓桿與擁擠部位平倉。兩者對固定收益的意義不同：科技投資若持久減少，將影響企業發債與成長預期；若股市迅速復甦，聯準會政策與美債供給便會重新成為殖利率的主要驅動因素。

overall_summary.headline: 晶片股重挫、油價回落緩和近期升息預期，美債小幅走高
overall_summary.session_narrative:
全球半導體類股遭到拋售、油價下跌，加上市場質疑聯準會升息時點，促使買盤在前一交易日下跌後回流；截至6月23日紐約收盤，美債小幅上漲。2年期殖利率下降2.9個基點至4.199%，5年期下降1.9個基點至4.269%，10年期下降1.2個基點至4.498%，30年期微降0.2個基點至4.947%。前端領漲使2s10s陡峭化1.7個基點。

相較股市受到的衝擊，美債漲幅有限：那斯達克100指數下跌3.29%，半導體指數重挫7.87%，VIX則上升12.79%。美債獲得避險買盤，但美元升至7個月高點，交換市場仍反映截至2027年年中約45個基點的升息幅度。隨荷莫茲海峽油輪活動變得更為明顯，油價下跌降低未來能源壓力。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降3個基點至2.219%，實質殖利率則上升1.8個基點至2.279%，顯示推動名目債上漲的是通膨補償下降，而非實質金融情勢轉向寬鬆。

6月調查數據強化了暫緩立即升息的理由，卻未消除通膨疑慮：全國產出加快，但就業轉弱，銷售價格與供應壓力指標仍令人不安。規模$690億的2年期美債標售需求強勁，證實買方願意在目前殖利率附近增加政策敏感型債券部位。SpaceX也完成首筆$250億債券發行，但其2036年期債券的利差較美債高1.4個百分點，顯示企業債投資人仍要求可觀補償，以承擔長期現金流風險。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries advanced modestly on June 23 as a global semiconductor rout, lower oil prices and doubts about the timing of Federal Reserve increases brought buyers back after the previous session’s selloff. The 2-year yield fell 2.9 basis points to 4.199%, the 5-year declined 1.9 basis points to 4.269%, the 10-year eased 1.2 basis points to 4.498% and the 30-year slipped 0.2 basis point to 4.947%. The front-end lead steepened 2s10s by 1.7 basis points to 29.9 basis points and 2s30s by 2.7 basis points to 74.8 basis points.

The rally was restrained relative to the shock in equities. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 3.29%, the PHLX Semiconductor Index plunged 7.87% and the S&P 500 lost 1.44%, while the VIX rose 12.79% to 19.49. South Korea’s Kospi had already fallen 10% as leveraged selling amplified losses in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix. Treasuries attracted a haven bid, but the market did not abandon the Fed’s more restrictive policy path: swaps still implied about 45 basis points of tightening by mid-2027, and the dollar index rose 0.39% to a 7-month high.

Oil supplied a second source of relief. WTI declined 2.15% to $73.21 and Brent fell 1.05% to $77.08 as tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz became more visible following the interim U.S.-Iran peace arrangement. The 10-year breakeven inflation rate fell 3 basis points to 2.219%, while the 10-year real yield rose 1.8 basis points to 2.279%. Nominal Treasuries therefore rallied because inflation compensation declined by more than real yields increased, a composition consistent with lower prospective energy pressure but continued demand for a high inflation-adjusted return.

Fresh U.S. surveys did not resolve that tension. The S&P Global flash composite PMI strengthened to 52.2 in June, led by manufacturing, yet employment fell for a second month and factory job losses were the sharpest since 2020. Regional surveys were weaker, while delivery delays and selling-price measures remained uncomfortable for a Fed newly focused on restoring price stability. Traders reduced the most aggressive near-term increase wagers without rejecting the possibility of higher rates later in the year.

Primary markets reinforced that distinction. A $69 billion 2-year Treasury auction drew strong demand at 4.189%, while SpaceX completed a $25 billion debut bond sale only after paying a meaningful premium over comparable investment-grade debt. The two transactions showed that buyers would commit capital at the new yield structure, but corporate investors required compensation for cash-flow risk that an equity valuation alone could not remove.

## Risk Aversion Brings a Limited Treasury Rally

The Treasury move began with a rapid deterioration in the global technology trade. A modest decline in South Korean shares developed into a 10% fall in the Kospi, triggering a circuit breaker as foreign investors sold more than $2.5 billion of stocks. Samsung and SK Hynix each lost more than 12%, and market participants cited forced liquidation by leveraged retail investors and selling connected with geared exchange-traded products.

The pressure spread to U.S. chipmakers. The semiconductor index, which had more than doubled from its war-driven lows, fell nearly 8%; Micron Technology dropped 13% before earnings scheduled for June 24. The Nasdaq 100’s 3.3% decline left it down for the week but still higher for the year, making the session a sharp reversal within a large preceding rally rather than evidence by itself of a broader economic contraction.

The catalyst mattered for bonds because investors were reassessing both the prospective returns on artificial-intelligence spending and the discount rate applied to those returns. The sector had benefited from expectations of vast infrastructure demand, but rising Fed-rate expectations made long-duration equity valuations harder to sustain. The selloff consequently generated a haven bid in Treasuries while also illustrating the tighter financial conditions produced by the post-FOMC increase in real yields.

SpaceX shares captured that instability. The stock closed 1% higher at $156.11 after falling as much as 4.8% and rising as much as 7.1% intraday. The gain ended a 3-day decline that had erased more than $600 billion of market value, but did not reverse the broader concern about the funding required for AI, satellite and orbital-computing projects.

Credit-fund prices were more stable than equities. The LQD investment-grade fund gained 0.12%, while HYG and JNK slipped 0.09% and 0.05%, respectively. The EMB emerging-market debt fund declined 0.15%. Those small moves indicated that the technology shock had not developed into indiscriminate selling across publicly traded bond funds by the close.

Treasury turnover increased as the risk reversal unfolded. FINRA recorded $1.132 trillion of par activity, 14.2% more than on June 22, while nominal-coupon activity rose 16.1% to $855.7 billion. Activity in nominal coupons with no more than 2 years remaining increased 35.5% to $239.8 billion. The figures measure two-way trading rather than investor direction, but the concentration at the front end was consistent with the day’s reassessment of Fed timing and the new 2-year auction.

The resulting curve move was a partial reversal of the preceding week’s flattening, not a return to an easy-policy outlook. The 2-year yield remained 14.4 basis points higher over the week, compared with increases of 5.8 basis points in the 10-year and only 0.3 basis point in the 30-year. The 2s10s curve was still 8.6 basis points flatter over that period and 13.7 basis points flatter over the month.

Options activity showed why the cash rally remained measured. Trading in Secured Overnight Financing Rate contracts doubled immediately after the Fed’s June decision, with many positions designed to benefit from fewer increases than money markets had begun to imply. That activity continued into the new week. TD Securities strategist Molly Brooks judged expectations of an increase as early as July excessive even if higher rates later in the year remained plausible, because officials could wait for additional labor and inflation evidence.

Investors also bought options protecting against a larger Treasury rally. Nearly $30 million was spent across Monday and Tuesday on August calls that would benefit if the 10-year yield moved toward 4.4% or below. A JPMorgan client survey showed neutral Treasury positions rising 4 percentage points to their highest level in about 2 months, while both long and short shares declined by 2 percentage points. That combination described uncertainty over timing more clearly than a wholesale rejection of the Fed’s hawkish turn.

The dollar’s strength provided the other side of the policy signal. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index rose 0.4% to its highest close since November, supported by the prospect of almost two quarter-point Fed increases by early 2027 and by weaker policy expectations elsewhere. The euro fell as low as $1.1376, while the yen remained under pressure beyond 160 per dollar. The simultaneous rise in Treasuries and the dollar was therefore compatible with a risk-off session in which U.S. rate expectations eased marginally from elevated levels but remained high relative to those in other economies.

Oil’s decline reduced one reason for an immediate Fed response. More visible tanker traffic through Hormuz suggested that the interim peace arrangement was improving physical flows, while the U.S. had granted Iran a 60-day license to sell oil internationally. The diplomacy remained incomplete. President Donald Trump said $12 billion expected to be released from frozen Iranian accounts could be used only for food and medical purchases from the U.S.; Iranian officials said the money could be used freely. Iran and Oman also said they would work on a future arrangement for administering the strait, including the unresolved possibility of transit charges.

The market treated those disputes as qualifications to an improving supply picture rather than a renewed interruption. Crude’s decline brought WTI’s 1-month loss to 24.21% and Brent’s to 25.56%. Gold futures fell 1.24% to $4,129.90, extending their monthly decline to 8.65%, as higher real yields and a stronger dollar outweighed the day’s demand for safety.

## Business Surveys Mix Faster Output With Weaker Labor

The June flash U.S. PMI provided the strongest current activity signal. The composite output index rose to 52.2 from 51.5, with readings above 50 indicating expansion. Services business activity increased to 51.3 from 50.7, while the manufacturing PMI climbed to 55.7 from 55.1 and the manufacturing-output index rose to 57.7 from 56.6.

The acceleration was not uniformly reassuring. Employment declined for a second consecutive month across the survey, and factory headcount contracted at the fastest pace since 2020. Supplier delays were the most widespread since August 2022, reflecting continuing supply disruption and inventory building. Input-cost inflation eased only modestly from an elevated level, while output-price inflation remained at May’s high pace.

The combination matters for the reaction function because faster output did not bring stronger employment or cleaner disinflation. Manufacturers were benefiting from demand and precautionary inventory accumulation, but longer delivery times and still-elevated selling prices left open the possibility that supply pressure would persist. At the same time, the employment decline argued against treating stronger factory production as sufficient evidence for an immediate increase in rates.

Regional reports leaned more clearly toward softer activity. The Richmond Fed manufacturing composite fell to 4 in June from 13. Shipments dropped to 3 from 16, new orders to 9 from 17 and employment to -1 from 3. Local business conditions turned negative at -3 from 5, although expectations for future local conditions improved to 23 from 17. Future employment expectations weakened to 16 from 23, and firms reported a notable acceleration in prices paid.

The Philadelphia Fed’s nonmanufacturing survey showed a different mix. Firm-level general activity turned positive at 2.4 from -3.8, and sales or revenues rebounded to 19.6 from -7.6. New orders remained slightly negative at -0.7, compared with -0.8, while full-time employment deteriorated to -4.8 from -1.1. The 6-month firm outlook fell to -0.3 from 14.4.

Price measures within that survey split. Prices paid eased to 25.8 from 36.5, but prices received rose to 20.2 from 13.1. Regional general activity remained deeply negative at -25.8, compared with -23.6. The rebound in company sales was therefore accompanied by weaker hiring, poorer expectations and firmer realized selling prices.

Together, the releases offered no single growth or inflation message. The national PMI suggested faster expansion, especially in manufacturing, while the Richmond report showed broad deceleration and the Philadelphia services survey showed improved sales without stronger orders or labor. The common feature was the weakness in employment. The less favorable bond-market feature was that price pressure remained visible despite lower oil.

That divergence helped explain why short Treasuries outperformed without producing a larger rally. Evidence of weaker hiring and uneven regional demand challenged the case for raising rates immediately, while elevated output prices, supply delays and faster Richmond prices paid preserved the case for keeping policy restrictive. With about 45 basis points of tightening still implied by mid-2027, the market’s adjustment was primarily about when the Fed might act, not whether the inflation risk had disappeared.

The 10-year inflation decomposition sharpened the distinction. Breakeven inflation fell to 2.219%, down 8.7 basis points over the week and 19.4 basis points over the month, as oil’s retreat reduced compensation for future price increases. The real yield nevertheless reached 2.279%, 14.5 basis points higher over the week and 13.3 basis points higher over the month. Investors were attaching less inflation premium to a 10-year nominal bond while demanding a substantially higher real return than before the June policy repricing.

## Treasury Auctions Find Demand at Higher Front-End Yields

The $69 billion 2-year note auction produced the clearest evidence that buyers were willing to add policy-sensitive duration at current levels. The sale stopped at 4.189%, below the yield expected immediately before bidding and therefore indicative of strong demand. It was still the highest 2-year auction yield since January 2025.

The result came less than a week after Chair Kevin Warsh’s first post-meeting press conference drove a sharp rise in front-end yields and encouraged markets to price almost 50 basis points of tightening over the following year. By the June 23 close, the 2-year yield was around 4.20%, leaving the auction close to prevailing levels but with enough yield to attract investors seeking protection against a less aggressive path than the market had recently considered.

The sale was the first fixed-rate coupon auction of a 3-day sequence. Treasury is due to sell $70 billion of new 5-year notes on June 24 and $44 billion of new 7-year notes on June 25. The strong 2-year result established demand for the maturity most directly linked to the policy rate, but did not settle whether investors would show the same appetite for the belly of the curve, where term premium, real yields and corporate hedging can play larger roles.

That distinction was visible before the auction cycle. Five- and 10-year yields had risen on June 22 despite lower oil, and traders attributed part of the move to rate hedging associated with SpaceX’s jumbo bond financing. Such hedging can temporarily add selling pressure in Treasuries before a large corporate deal prices. Once the financing and the 2-year auction were completed, that pressure was less acute, but the upcoming 5- and 7-year sales left the intermediate sector exposed to further supply tests.

Treasury’s separate $65 billion 42-day bill auction stopped at a 3.620% high rate and a 3.686% investment rate. The bid-to-cover ratio was 2.91. Indirect bidders received 65.67% of accepted competitive tenders, primary dealers took 32.04% and direct bidders 2.29%; Treasury allotted 92.35% of bids submitted at the high rate.

The result established absorption at the 6-week point but offered no basis for judging a tail or through because no when-issued reference was available. The securities settle and are issued on June 25 and mature August 6. The sale added $65 billion of short-bill supply without producing evidence of front-end funding stress or a conflict with the modest coupon rally.

Cash-market activity also showed that the session involved more than auction mechanics. Nominal-coupon par volume increased across several sectors, including a 10.9% rise in maturities above 3 and through 5 years and a 16% increase beyond 20 years. TIPS activity rose 4.7% to $28.8 billion. The broad increase in turnover accompanied an equity shock, a policy repricing and primary supply, rather than reflecting one isolated auction response.

## SpaceX Pays a Premium for Its $25 Billion Debut

SpaceX raised $25 billion in a 5-part investment-grade bond sale, converting the previous day’s marketing exercise into one of the largest corporate debuts on record. Demand reached almost $90 billion at its peak and stood at about $73 billion when the transaction priced. The final book was less than 3 times the amount offered, below the roughly 4-times average for high-grade transactions this year.

The company’s 2036 bonds priced 1.4 percentage points above Treasuries, about 0.4 percentage point wider than the average spread on similarly rated BBB debt. The concession showed that investment-grade ratings and SpaceX’s roughly $2 trillion equity value did not eliminate creditor concerns about the scale and duration of its capital program.

Demand was strongest for the shortest-dated and least risky tranche. That preference aligned with the principal fixed-income concern: bondholders receive coupon and principal but do not participate fully if satellite networks, artificial intelligence or data centers in space generate exceptional equity returns. They remain exposed if construction costs rise, cash generation takes longer than expected or the company chooses to protect expansion plans over creditors’ preferred pace of deleveraging.

The ratings provide room, but not unanimity about the risk. Moody’s assigned SpaceX Baa1, the same grade it initially gave Nvidia nearly a decade ago when that company had a lighter debt load and positive free cash flow. S&P expects SpaceX to continue burning cash through 2030, with the burn rate increasing sharply in 2027 as expenditure grows faster than revenue.

SpaceX had more than $100 billion of cash on June 19 and has said it intends to maintain investment-grade ratings. Ratings firms have identified several potential defenses, including slowing investment or raising additional equity. Those options reduce near-term liquidity risk, but they do not remove the uncertainty over how much debt will ultimately be required for the company’s ambitions.

The order book nevertheless demonstrated substantial access to capital. Investors accepted $25 billion of exposure during a day when technology equities were falling sharply, Treasury real yields remained elevated and doubts about AI valuations were spreading across regions. The financing window was open; the 140-basis-point spread on the 2036 maturity was the price of using it at such scale.

Recent performance in other technology bonds encouraged that caution. Nvidia had raised $25 billion the preceding week and attracted as much as $85 billion of orders, but its securities were subsequently trading somewhat weaker relative to Treasuries. SpaceX’s smaller final coverage ratio and preference for the shortest tranche suggested that buyers were discriminating among technology borrowers rather than treating the AI theme as sufficient credit support.

The contrast with the equity market was especially sharp. SpaceX’s stock recovered 1% on June 23 after a 3-day decline, but its intraday swings remained large. Equity holders could value the probability of extraordinary growth; creditors focused on contractual cash flows, leverage and the time required for projects to produce returns. The bond premium represented that asymmetry more directly than the company’s share price.

## Europe and Japan Confront Different Inflation Constraints

Euro-area data presented the ECB with a milder contraction but no return to growth. The flash composite PMI increased to 49.5 in June from 48.5, remaining below 50 for a third month. Services improved to 48.9 from 47.7, while the manufacturing PMI eased to 51.3 from 51.6 and manufacturing output slipped to 51.2 from 51.3. Employment declined fractionally.

Price pressure moderated more clearly than activity recovered. Input-cost inflation slowed to its weakest pace since February, and output-price inflation was the lowest in 3 months. That combination helped traders reduce ECB increase expectations and contributed to the euro’s decline, even as policymakers continued to warn that the accumulated energy shock could keep inflation above target into 2027.

ECB Chief Economist Philip Lane said forward-looking indicators pointed to price pressure in coming months and warned that inflation could remain above 2% for “quite some time.” He described the June rate increase as a measured response even under the ECB’s milder Middle East scenario. Lane also said wages retained some momentum and were likely to rise faster than inflation for the average worker this year, while acknowledging that growth risks were tilted downward.

Vice President Boris Vujcic defended the June increase as robust across the ECB’s scenarios because both headline and core inflation were expected to remain higher for longer. His qualification was that medium- and long-term expectations remained anchored and compensation per employee was slowing, with no current evidence of wage second-round effects.

Spanish central-bank Governor Jose Luis Escrivá emphasized a different channel. He said oil costs were already passing through production chains into transport, food and other goods and argued that policy had to consider the effect on the more persistent components of inflation into 2027. The remarks reinforced the distinction between weaker current business activity and an inflation process that may outlast the initial energy surge.

The mixed policy communication widened the contrast with the Fed. The dollar index reached a 7-month high, while the euro fell to its weakest level in about a year during the session. One-year euro-dollar risk reversals moved to their strongest preference for euro puts since before the 2025 U.S. tariff announcement. The currency market was pricing a greater probability that U.S. rates would rise relative to euro-area rates, even though ECB officials had not declared their tightening work complete.

Hungary moved in the opposite direction. The National Bank of Hungary reduced its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 6%, matching 20 of 21 economist forecasts. Governor Mihaly Varga said there was room for two more quarter-point reductions during the summer before policymakers reassess their room in September, describing the sequence as a “mini” easing cycle.

The central bank cut its forecast for average 2026 inflation to 1.8% from 3.8% in March. It expects inflation to rise to 2.3% in 2027 and reach its 3% target in 2028. A stronger forint had reduced imported inflation and allowed Hungary to diverge from the ECB and the Czech central bank despite the broader energy shock.

The currency fell as much as 1.3% against the euro after the decision, its largest decline since March, reducing its year-to-date gain to about 8%. Even after the cut, Hungary’s 6% benchmark remained well above the 3.75% rates in Poland and the Czech Republic. The reaction showed that the easing room depended partly on preserving the currency gains that had created it.

Japan’s sovereign market provided a less comfortable demand signal. A 5-year JGB auction produced a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.11, down from 3.22 at the previous sale and below the 12-month average of 3.47. The auction tail widened to 0.06 from 0.04, and bond futures trimmed gains after the result.

The soft demand came as the yen traded beyond 160 per dollar and investors debated whether the Bank of Japan would need to increase rates again to contain imported inflation. Overnight-index swaps implied less than one additional 25-basis-point move for the rest of 2026. The auction suggested that buyers still required compensation for the risk that yen weakness and persistent inflation would force a faster path.

A hypothetical European regulatory change added a separate structural issue for Treasuries. Research by economists at the Kiel Institute estimated that applying a 20% risk weight to U.S. government debt held by European banks and insurers could reduce demand by about $200 billion over a decade and add as much as $42 billion a year to U.S. fiscal costs through higher yields. The exercise was a research scenario, not an announced policy, but it quantified how regulatory treatment could matter for the foreign demand base without requiring coordinated sovereign selling.

## Forward Market Significance

Australia’s May monthly CPI is due at 11:30 in Sydney on June 24. The previous readings showed prices rising 0.4% on the month and 4.2% from a year earlier. Headline and trimmed-mean inflation will determine whether the energy retreat is providing enough relief to validate the Reserve Bank of Australia’s restrictive stance.

U.S. new-home sales follow at 10:00 ET, after an annualized April pace of 622,000, for-sale inventory of 489,000 and 9.4 months of supply. The report will update the effect of elevated mortgage rates on demand, prices and housing inventory.

Treasury’s June 24 supply begins with a $28 billion reopening of a 2-year floating-rate note at 11:30 ET, carrying a 0.103% spread and settling June 26. A 119-day bill auction is scheduled at the same time. The larger test comes at 13:00, when Treasury sells $70 billion of new 5-year notes maturing June 30, 2031. The result will show whether the demand evident in the 2-year sale extends into a sector that has absorbed both higher real yields and corporate-rate hedging.

Japan reopens about ¥700 billion of 20-year JGBs on June 25, with the result expected around 12:35 in Tokyo. The auction follows the weaker 5-year sale and will test whether concerns over the BOJ path and yen depreciation are producing still-greater resistance in super-long duration.

The principal U.S. data cluster arrives at 08:30 ET on June 25. Initial claims are expected at 225,000 after 226,000, with continuing claims previously at 1.810 million. The release will help determine whether the employment weakness in the June business surveys is becoming visible in layoffs or remains concentrated in hiring and company staffing plans.

Advance durable-goods orders are expected to fall 5% in May after a 7.9% increase in April. Transportation is likely to dominate the headline, making the ex-transportation and capital-goods details more informative for business investment. The third estimate of Q1 GDP is expected at 1.7% annualized, compared with the prior 1.6%, while revisions to PCE prices will refine the inflation starting point.

Personal income and outlays will carry the greatest policy significance. Expectations call for income to rise 0.4%, spending 0.6%, headline PCE prices 0.5% and core PCE prices 0.3% on the month. A firm core reading alongside resilient real spending would support the Fed’s restrictive bias and challenge options positions favoring fewer increases. Softer inflation or consumption, especially alongside weaker labor evidence, would strengthen the case for waiting beyond July.

Treasury completes the coupon cycle at 13:00 ET on June 25 with $44 billion of new 7-year notes maturing June 30, 2033. Four- and 8-week bill sales precede it at 11:30. Bidder participation and dealer awards in the 5- and 7-year auctions will indicate whether Tuesday’s front-end demand was maturity-specific or part of broader willingness to absorb duration near current yields.

Banco de México announces its June decision at 15:00 ET on June 25. The overnight target is 6.50%, and the expected outcome is no change. Energy inflation, peso sensitivity to the stronger dollar and the turn toward tighter global policy will determine whether the bank continues to treat its easing cycle as closed.

The final June University of Michigan survey is due June 26 at 10:00 ET. Preliminary sentiment was 48.9, with current conditions at 48.4 and expectations at 49.3. Revisions to sentiment and inflation expectations will show whether cheaper oil is beginning to improve household views or whether the earlier price shock remains embedded.

Micron’s results provide the nearer market test after the semiconductor rout. Its earnings and demand commentary will indicate whether the selloff reflects a reassessment of AI infrastructure orders or primarily the unwinding of leverage and crowded positioning. The distinction matters for fixed income because a durable reduction in technology investment would affect corporate issuance and growth expectations, while a rapid equity recovery would leave the Fed and Treasury supply as the dominant drivers of yields.

section_summaries.summary: Short Treasuries led a modest rally as the semiconductor rout generated haven demand and falling oil reduced inflation compensation. The move remained restrained because real yields rose, the dollar strengthened and markets retained about 45 basis points of Fed tightening by mid-2027. Mixed U.S. surveys weakened the case for an immediate increase without removing price risks, while the 2-year auction and SpaceX financing showed that capital remained available at the new yield structure—but on different terms for sovereign and corporate risk.

section_summaries.summary: The euro-area composite PMI improved to 49.5 but remained in contraction, while price pressures moderated and traders reduced ECB increase expectations. Officials nevertheless warned that energy effects could keep inflation above target into 2027. Hungary cut its benchmark rate to 6% as a stronger forint reduced imported inflation, but the currency weakened after the decision. In Japan, a softer 5-year JGB auction and yen weakness beyond 160 per dollar showed that buyers still required compensation for the risk of a faster BOJ path.

The next tests divide between policy evidence and duration demand. U.S. claims, durable-goods details, GDP revisions and personal income and outlays will show whether weaker survey employment is reaching layoffs and whether core inflation and spending sustain the Fed’s restrictive bias. The 5- and 7-year Treasury auctions will test whether strong 2-year demand extends along the curve. Micron’s results will help distinguish weaker AI infrastructure demand from an unwind of leveraged equity positioning.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries edge higher as the chip rout and cheaper oil soften near-term Fed expectations
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries advanced modestly at the June 23 NY close as a global semiconductor selloff, lower oil and doubts about the timing of Federal Reserve increases restored demand after the previous session’s decline. The 2-year yield fell 2.9 basis points to 4.199%, the 5-year declined 1.9 basis points to 4.269%, the 10-year eased 1.2 basis points to 4.498% and the 30-year slipped 0.2 basis point to 4.947%. The front-end lead steepened 2s10s by 1.7 basis points.

The rally was limited relative to the equity shock: the Nasdaq 100 lost 3.29%, the semiconductor index fell 7.87% and the VIX rose 12.79%. Treasuries received a haven bid, but the dollar reached a 7-month high and swaps still implied about 45 basis points of tightening by mid-2027. Oil’s decline as Hormuz tanker traffic became more visible reduced prospective energy pressure. The 10-year breakeven fell 3 basis points to 2.219%, while the real yield rose 1.8 basis points to 2.279%, showing that lower inflation compensation—not easier real financial conditions—drove the nominal rally.

June surveys strengthened the case for delaying an immediate increase without resolving inflation concerns: national output accelerated, but employment weakened and selling-price and supply-pressure measures remained uncomfortable. Strong demand at the $69 billion 2-year auction confirmed buyers would add policy-sensitive duration near current yields. SpaceX also completed a $25 billion bond debut, but its 2036 debt priced 1.4 percentage points above Treasuries, showing that corporate investors still required substantial compensation for long-horizon cash-flow risk.
overall_summary.summary: A semiconductor-led equity rout and falling crude brought a modest haven bid led by short Treasuries, but elevated real yields, persistent price pressure and roughly 45 basis points of tightening still implied by mid-2027 kept the rally restrained.
